cond_0001.intro: The Peptide group within Global Discovery Chemistry group is committed to the delivery of high-quality drug candidates working across all Therapeutic Areas (TAs). This mission requires deep scientific expertise in a number of disciplines including chemistry, cellular and molecular pharmacology, enzymology, and screening technologies coupled with an ability to work collaboratively with internal and external partners. We are seeking an experienced, highly skilled, and motivated chemist with excellent peptide chemistry and medicinal chemistry expertise to shepherd peptide drug discovery programs and advance them toward the clinic. This position will require the candidate to possess and leverage deep knowledge and capabilities to deliver differentiated clinical candidates to the [Company name masked] product development pipeline within our Disease and Pathway Area Stronghold (DAS and PAS) strategy. Using a mix of internal and external resources, the Principal Scientist will partner with key stakeholders in the TAs and other internal groups, represent medicinal chemistry, lead cross-functional project teams, and be co-responsible for building, managing, and delivering high quality clinical molecules.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Of the Principal Scientist will include:
As a dynamic medicinal chemist, drive and contribute to the peptide chemistry function for one or more drug discovery projects, working in concert with partners in molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, computational chemistry, chemistry capabilities, ADME, structural biology, chemical development, and other key functions. Work collaboratively with other [Company name masked] drug discovery sites, including [Location masked], [Location masked], [Location masked], and [Location masked], and with [Company name masked] Innovation Centers worldwide. Analyze synthetic routes to designed compounds, screening data, perform literature reviews, design, propose, and execute medicinal chemistry plans, coordinate chemistry and biology data to support compound progression and patent strategies. Independently designing and synthesizing drug-like peptide molecules utilizing current medicinal chemistry knowledge, including property-based optimization, and an understanding of ADME, pharmacokinetics and optimal physicochemical properties. Provide scientific direction and leadership for synthetic and medicinal chemistry activities of internal FTEs. This role may have direct people management responsibilities. Supervise and direct synthetic chemistry activities at contract research organizations (CROs). Contribute to portfolio and stage-gate reviews, lead the preparation and presentation of dossiers for clinical candidate nomination and compound advancement. Participate in shaping and implementing strategies that support synthetic and medicinal chemistry growth objectives at [Company name masked], including academic relations and talent acquisition. Ensure optimal interaction/communication and provide updates on project status to drug discovery leadership. Maintain a significant level of productivity in the laboratory setting.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD in peptide, synthetic organic, or medicinal chemistry.
A minimum of 3 or more years' experience in the biopharmaceutical industry with a proven track record of key contributions to innovative peptide projects impacting the trajectory of programs leading to Go/NoGo decisions and/or clinical candidate selection.
Experience designing peptide conformational restraints to influence secondary structure (ie. A-helices, b-turn induction & mimicry, sidechain modifications) using computational modeling tools.
Good understanding of cellular/molecular biology, biochemistry, disease pharmacology, mechanisms of drug metabolism and molecular toxicology, pharmaco-kinetic and pharmaco-dynamic sciences, and formulations for the in vivo evaluation of drug candidates.
Knowledge of and/or experience with computational chemistry methods and biophysical techniques such as X-ray crystallography and macromolecular NMR.
Strong problem-solving skills for developing creative, innovative solutions, and meeting project objectives.
Demonstrated influence, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills, including the ability to succeed within a matrix environment.
Design and synthesis of constrained macrocycles, de-peptidization strategies including back-bone modifications and peptidomimetics.
Preferred Requirements
Broad experience and proven accomplishments in medicinal chemistry; experience in one or more therapeutic areas.
Demonstrated operational skills for contributing to discovery programs at the level of a senior chemist/team leader.
Experience in peptide hit finding approaches – phage display, mRNA display technologies, etc.
Cell penetrating peptides.
Permeable and orally bioavailable peptides.
Intracellular protein-protein interaction targets.
Chemical biology using cyclic peptide scaffolds.
Strong track record of scientific contributions including peer reviewed first-author publications, patent applications, and presentations at major national meetings.

We are looking for a Principal Scientist to join our Global Discovery Chemistry team.
The Peptide group within Global Discovery Chemistry is committed to delivering high-quality drug candidates across all Therapeutic Areas (TAs). This mission requires deep scientific expertise across chemistry, cellular and molecular pharmacology, enzymology, and screening technologies, along with the ability to work with internal and external partners.
We are seeking an experienced, highly skilled chemist with strong peptide chemistry and medicinal chemistry expertise to own peptide drug discovery programs and drive them toward the clinic. This position requires deep knowledge and capabilities to deliver differentiated clinical candidates to the [Company name masked] product development pipeline within our Disease and Pathway Area Stronghold (DAS and PAS) strategy. Using a mix of internal and external resources, the Principal Scientist will lead coordination with key stakeholders in the TAs and other internal groups, represent medicinal chemistry, direct cross-functional project teams, and take accountability for building, managing, and delivering high-quality clinical molecules.
cond_0008.responsibilities: As a dynamic medicinal chemist, lead and execute the peptide chemistry function for one or more drug discovery projects, working in concert with partners in molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, computational chemistry, chemistry capabilities, ADME, structural biology, chemical development, and other key functions. Drive collaboration with other [Company name masked] drug discovery sites, including [Location masked], and with [Company name masked] Innovation Centers worldwide. Analyze synthetic routes to designed compounds, screening data, perform literature reviews, design, propose, and execute medicinal chemistry plans, and direct chemistry and biology data to support compound progression and patent strategies. Independently design and synthesize drug-like peptide molecules utilizing current medicinal chemistry knowledge, including property-based optimization, and an understanding of ADME, pharmacokinetics, and optimal physicochemical properties. Provide scientific direction and leadership for synthetic and medicinal chemistry activities of internal FTEs. This role may have direct people management responsibilities. Direct synthetic chemistry activities at contract research organizations (CROs). Contribute to portfolio and stage-gate reviews, lead the preparation and presentation of dossiers for clinical candidate nomination and compound advancement. Take ownership of shaping and implementing strategies that support synthetic and medicinal chemistry growth objectives at [Company name masked], including academic relations and talent acquisition. Ensure optimal interaction and communication, and deliver updates on project status to drug discovery leadership. Maintain a significant level of productivity in the laboratory setting.
cond_0008.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD in peptide, synthetic organic, or medicinal chemistry.
A minimum of 3 or more years' experience in the biopharmaceutical industry with a proven track record of key contributions to innovative peptide projects impacting the trajectory of programs leading to Go/NoGo decisions and/or clinical candidate selection.
Experience designing peptide conformational restraints to influence secondary structure (i.e. A-helices, b-turn induction & mimicry, sidechain modifications) using computational modeling tools.
Good understanding of cellular/molecular biology, biochemistry, disease pharmacology, mechanisms of drug metabolism and molecular toxicology, pharmaco-kinetic and pharmaco-dynamic sciences, and formulations for the in vivo evaluation of drug candidates.
Knowledge of and/or experience with computational chemistry methods and biophysical techniques such as X-ray crystallography and macromolecular NMR.
Strong problem-solving skills for developing creative, innovative solutions and meeting project objectives.
Demonstrated influence, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills, including the ability to succeed within a matrix environment.
Design and synthesis of constrained macrocycles, de-peptidization strategies including back-bone modifications and peptidomimetics.
Preferred Requirements
Broad experience and proven accomplishments in medicinal chemistry; experience in one or more therapeutic areas.
Demonstrated operational skills for contributing to discovery programs at the level of a senior chemist/team leader.
Experience in peptide hit finding approaches – phage display, mRNA display technologies, etc.
Cell penetrating peptides.
Permeable and orally bioavailable peptides.
Intracellular protein-protein interaction targets.
Chemical biology using cyclic peptide scaffolds.
Strong track record of scientific contributions including peer reviewed first-author publications, patent applications, and presentations at major national meetings.

cond_0009.intro:
We are looking for a Principal Scientist to join our Global Discovery Chemistry team, working within the Peptide group in Medicinal Chemistry at [Location masked].
The Peptide group is committed to delivering high-quality drug candidates across all Therapeutic Areas (TAs). This work draws on deep scientific expertise in chemistry, cellular and molecular pharmacology, enzymology, and screening technologies, and depends on close collaboration with internal and external partners. We are seeking an experienced chemist with strong peptide and medicinal chemistry expertise to help shepherd peptide drug discovery programs toward the clinic. The Principal Scientist will work alongside key stakeholders in the TAs and other internal groups, represent medicinal chemistry in cross-functional project teams, and share responsibility for building, managing, and delivering high-quality clinical molecules.
cond_0009.responsibilities:
As a medicinal chemist, you will contribute to the peptide chemistry function for one or more drug discovery projects, working in concert with partners in molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, computational chemistry, ADME, structural biology, chemical development, and other key functions. You will coordinate with other [Company name masked] drug discovery sites and Innovation Centers worldwide.
Working together with the team, you will:
Analyze synthetic routes to designed compounds, review screening data and literature, and help shape and execute medicinal chemistry plans; coordinate chemistry and biology data to support compound progression and patent strategies.
Collaborate on the design and synthesis of drug-like peptide molecules, applying current medicinal chemistry knowledge including property-based optimization and an understanding of ADME, pharmacokinetics, and physicochemical properties.
Provide scientific direction for synthetic and medicinal chemistry activities of internal FTEs. This role may include direct people management responsibilities.
Coordinate and oversee synthetic chemistry activities at contract research organizations (CROs).
Contribute to portfolio and stage-gate reviews; help prepare and present dossiers for clinical candidate nomination and compound advancement.
Support the shaping and implementation of strategies for synthetic and medicinal chemistry growth, including academic relations and talent acquisition.
Share updates on project status with drug discovery leadership and help ensure clear communication across the team.
Maintain a meaningful level of hands-on productivity in the laboratory.
cond_0009.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD in peptide, synthetic organic, or medicinal chemistry.
At least 3 years of experience in the biopharmaceutical industry with a proven track record of contributions to innovative peptide projects, including impact on Go/NoGo decisions and/or clinical candidate selection.
Experience designing peptide conformational restraints to influence secondary structure (e.g., α-helices, β-turn induction and mimicry, sidechain modifications) using computational modeling tools.
Knowledge of and/or experience with computational chemistry methods and biophysical techniques such as X-ray crystallography and macromolecular NMR.
Design and synthesis of constrained macrocycles, de-peptidization strategies including backbone modifications and peptidomimetics.
Good understanding of cellular/molecular biology, biochemistry, disease pharmacology, mechanisms of drug metabolism and molecular toxicology, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic sciences, and formulations for in vivo evaluation of drug candidates.
Strong problem-solving skills for developing creative, innovative solutions and meeting project objectives.
Demonstrated influence, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills, including the ability to work effectively within a matrix environment.
Preferred Requirements
Broad experience and accomplishments in medicinal chemistry; experience in one or more therapeutic areas.
Demonstrated operational skills for contributing to discovery programs at the level of a senior chemist or team leader.
Experience in peptide hit-finding approaches such as phage display and mRNA display technologies.
Experience with cell-penetrating peptides, permeable and orally bioavailable peptides, intracellular protein-protein interaction targets, and chemical biology using cyclic peptide scaffolds.
Strong track record of scientific contributions including peer-reviewed first-author publications, patent applications, and presentations at major national meetings.

We are looking for a Principal Scientist to join our Peptide group in Medicinal Chemistry at [Location masked].
The Peptide group within [Company name masked]'s Global Discovery Chemistry group is committed to delivering high-quality drug candidates across all Therapeutic Areas (TAs). This mission requires deep scientific expertise across chemistry, cellular and molecular pharmacology, enzymology, and screening technologies, along with the ability to work collaboratively with internal and external partners.
We are seeking an experienced, skilled chemist with strong peptide chemistry and medicinal chemistry expertise to shepherd peptide drug discovery programs and advance them toward the clinic. The Principal Scientist will partner with key stakeholders in the TAs and other internal groups, represent medicinal chemistry, lead cross-functional project teams, and be co-responsible for building, managing, and delivering high quality clinical molecules. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of peptide drug discovery and the science behind program progression.
cond_0022.responsibilities:
Of the Principal Scientist will include:
As a medicinal chemist, drive and contribute to the peptide chemistry function for one or more drug discovery projects, working in concert with partners in molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, computational chemistry, chemistry capabilities, ADME, structural biology, chemical development, and other key functions.
Work collaboratively with other [Company name masked] drug discovery sites, including [Location masked], [Location masked], [Location masked], and [Location masked], and with [Company name masked] Innovation Centers worldwide.
Analyze synthetic routes to designed compounds, screening data, perform literature reviews, design, propose, and execute medicinal chemistry plans, coordinate chemistry and biology data to support compound progression and patent strategies.
Independently designing and synthesizing drug-like peptide molecules utilizing current medicinal chemistry knowledge, including property-based optimization, and an understanding of ADME, pharmacokinetics and optimal physicochemical properties.
Provide scientific direction and leadership for synthetic and medicinal chemistry activities of internal FTEs. This role may have direct people management responsibilities.
Supervise and direct synthetic chemistry activities at contract research organizations (CROs).
Contribute to portfolio and stage-gate reviews, lead the preparation and presentation of dossiers for clinical candidate nomination and compound advancement.
Participate in shaping and implementing strategies that support synthetic and medicinal chemistry growth objectives at [Company name masked], including academic relations and talent acquisition.
Ensure optimal interaction/communication and provide updates on project status to drug discovery leadership.
Maintain a significant level of productivity in the laboratory setting.
cond_0022.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD in peptide, synthetic organic, or medicinal chemistry.
A minimum of 3 or more years' experience in the biopharmaceutical industry with a proven track record of key contributions to innovative peptide projects impacting the trajectory of programs leading to Go/NoGo decisions and/or clinical candidate selection.
Experience designing peptide conformational restraints to influence secondary structure (ie. A-helices, b-turn induction & mimicry, sidechain modifications) using computational modeling tools.
Good understanding of cellular/molecular biology, biochemistry, disease pharmacology, mechanisms of drug metabolism and molecular toxicology, pharmaco-kinetic and pharmaco-dynamic sciences, and formulations for the in vivo evaluation of drug candidates.
Knowledge of and/or experience with computational chemistry methods and biophysical techniques such as X-ray crystallography and macromolecular NMR.
Strong problem-solving skills for developing creative, innovative solutions, and meeting project objectives.
Demonstrated influence, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills, including the ability to succeed within a matrix environment.
Design and synthesis of constrained macrocycles, de-peptidization strategies including back-bone modifications and peptidomimetics.
Preferred Requirements
Broad experience and proven accomplishments in medicinal chemistry; experience in one or more therapeutic areas.
Demonstrated operational skills for contributing to discovery programs at the level of a senior chemist/team leader.
Experience in peptide hit finding approaches – phage display, mRNA display technologies, etc.
Cell penetrating peptides.
Permeable and orally bioavailable peptides.
Intracellular protein-protein interaction targets.
Chemical biology using cyclic peptide scaffolds.
Strong track record of scientific contributions including peer reviewed first-author publications, patent applications, and presentations at major national meetings.

cond_0050.intro:
[Company name masked] is recruiting for a Principal Scientist in Global Discovery Chemistry, for our Peptide group in Medicinal Chemistry at our site in [Location masked].
The Peptide group within Global Discovery Chemistry group is committed to the delivery of high-quality drug candidates working across all Therapeutic Areas (TAs). This mission requires deep scientific expertise in a number of disciplines including chemistry, cellular and molecular pharmacology, enzymology, and screening technologies coupled with an ability to work collaboratively with internal and external partners. Building on a strong legacy of success, we are currently seeking an outstanding individual to join our team as Scientist, Discovery Chemistry.
We are seeking an experienced, highly skilled, and motivated chemist with excellent peptide chemistry and medicinal chemistry expertise to shepherd peptide drug discovery programs and advance them toward the clinic. This position will require the candidate to possess and leverage deep knowledge and capabilities to deliver differentiated clinical candidates to the [Company name masked] product development pipeline within our Disease and Pathway Area Stronghold (DAS and PAS) strategy. Using a mix of internal and external resources, the Principal Scientist will partner with key stakeholders in the TAs and other internal groups, represent medicinal chemistry, lead cross-functional project teams, and be co-responsible for building, managing, and delivering high quality clinical molecules. People usually grow into this role over time as they build experience with peptide drug discovery and medicinal chemistry work.
cond_0050.responsibilities:
Of the Principal Scientist will include:
As a dynamic medicinal chemist, drive and contribute to the peptide chemistry function for one or more drug discovery projects, working in concert with partners in molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, computational chemistry, chemistry capabilities, ADME, structural biology, chemical development, and other key functions. Work collaboratively with other [Company name masked] drug discovery sites, including [Location masked], [Location masked], [Location masked], and [Location masked], and with [Company name masked] Innovation Centers worldwide. Analyze synthetic routes to designed compounds, screening data, perform literature reviews, design, propose, and execute medicinal chemistry plans, coordinate chemistry and biology data to support compound progression and patent strategies. Independently designing and synthesizing drug-like peptide molecules utilizing current medicinal chemistry knowledge, including property-based optimization, and an understanding of ADME, pharmacokinetics and optimal physicochemical properties. Provide scientific direction and leadership for synthetic and medicinal chemistry activities of internal FTEs. This role may have direct people management responsibilities. Supervise and direct synthetic chemistry activities at contract research organizations (CROs). Contribute to portfolio and stage-gate reviews, lead the preparation and presentation of dossiers for clinical candidate nomination and compound advancement. Participate in shaping and implementing strategies that support synthetic and medicinal chemistry growth objectives at [Company name masked], including academic relations and talent acquisition. Ensure optimal interaction/communication and provide updates on project status to drug discovery leadership. Maintain a significant level of productivity in the laboratory setting.
cond_0050.requirements: PhD is required in peptide, synthetic organic, or medicinal chemistry. A minimum of 3 or more years' experience in the biopharmaceutical industry with a proven track record of key contributions to innovative peptide projects impacting the trajectory of programs leading to Go/NoGo decisions and/or clinical candidate selection. Broad experience and proven accomplishments in medicinal chemistry is preferred; experience in one or more therapeutic areas is preferred. Demonstrated operational skills for contributing to discovery programs at the level of a senior chemist/team leader are preferred. Experience designing peptide conformational restraints to influence secondary structure (ie. A-helices, b-turn induction & mimicry, sidechain modifications) using computational modeling tools is required. Good understanding of cellular/molecular biology, biochemistry, disease pharmacology, mechanisms of drug metabolism and molecular toxicology, pharmaco-kinetic and pharmaco-dynamic sciences, and formulations for the in vivo evaluation of drug candidates. Knowledge of and/or experience with computational chemistry methods and biophysical techniques such as X-ray crystallography and macromolecular NMR is required. Strong problem-solving skills for developing creative, innovative solutions, and meeting project objectives are required. Demonstrated influence, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills, including the ability to succeed within a matrix environment, are required. Design and synthesis of constrained macrocycles, de-peptidization strategies including back-bone modifications and peptidomimetics is required. Experience in peptide hit finding approaches – phage display, mRNA display technologies, etc. Cell penetrating peptides. Permeable and orally bioavailable peptides. Intracellular protein-protein interaction targets. Chemical biology using cyclic peptide scaffolds. Strong track record of scientific contributions including peer reviewed first-author publications, patent applications, and presentations at major national meetings is preferred.

cond_0159.intro:
We are looking for a Principal Scientist to join our Global Discovery Chemistry team.
The Peptide group within Global Discovery Chemistry is committed to delivering high-quality drug candidates across all Therapeutic Areas (TAs). This mission requires deep scientific expertise across chemistry, cellular and molecular pharmacology, enzymology, and screening technologies, along with the ability to work collaboratively with internal and external partners.
We are seeking an experienced, highly skilled chemist with strong peptide chemistry and medicinal chemistry expertise to shepherd peptide drug discovery programs and advance them toward the clinic. This position requires deep knowledge and capabilities to deliver differentiated clinical candidates to the [Company name masked] product development pipeline within our Disease and Pathway Area Stronghold (DAS and PAS) strategy. Using a mix of internal and external resources, the Principal Scientist will regularly connect with key stakeholders in the TAs and other internal groups, represent medicinal chemistry, lead cross-functional project teams, and be co-responsible for building, managing, and delivering high quality clinical molecules.
cond_0159.responsibilities:
Of the Principal Scientist will include:
As a medicinal chemist, actively drive and contribute to the peptide chemistry function for one or more drug discovery projects, working closely and regularly with partners in molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, computational chemistry, chemistry capabilities, ADME, structural biology, chemical development, and other key functions. Stay in regular contact and work collaboratively with other [Company name masked] drug discovery sites and with [Company name masked] Innovation Centers worldwide. Analyze synthetic routes to designed compounds, screening data, perform literature reviews, design, propose, and execute medicinal chemistry plans, and coordinate chemistry and biology data to support compound progression and patent strategies. Independently design and synthesize drug-like peptide molecules using current medicinal chemistry knowledge, including property-based optimization, and an understanding of ADME, pharmacokinetics, and optimal physicochemical properties. Provide scientific direction and leadership for synthetic and medicinal chemistry activities of internal FTEs. This role may have direct people management responsibilities. Supervise and direct synthetic chemistry activities at contract research organizations (CROs). Actively contribute to portfolio and stage-gate reviews, lead the preparation and presentation of dossiers for clinical candidate nomination and compound advancement. Participate in shaping and implementing strategies that support synthetic and medicinal chemistry growth objectives at [Company name masked], including academic relations and talent acquisition. Initiate and maintain clear communication and provide regular updates on project status to drug discovery leadership. Maintain a significant level of productivity in the laboratory setting.
cond_0159.requirements: PhD is required in peptide, synthetic organic, or medicinal chemistry. A minimum of 3 or more years' experience in the biopharmaceutical industry with a proven track record of key contributions to innovative peptide projects impacting the trajectory of programs leading to Go/NoGo decisions and/or clinical candidate selection. Broad experience and proven accomplishments in medicinal chemistry is preferred; experience in one or more therapeutic areas is preferred. Demonstrated operational skills for contributing to discovery programs at the level of a senior chemist/team leader are preferred. Experience designing peptide conformational restraints to influence secondary structure (ie. A-helices, b-turn induction & mimicry, sidechain modifications) using computational modeling tools is required. Good understanding of cellular/molecular biology, biochemistry, disease pharmacology, mechanisms of drug metabolism and molecular toxicology, pharmaco-kinetic and pharmaco-dynamic sciences, and formulations for the in vivo evaluation of drug candidates. Knowledge of and/or experience with computational chemistry methods and biophysical techniques such as X-ray crystallography and macromolecular NMR is required. Strong problem-solving skills for developing creative, innovative solutions, and meeting project objectives are required. Demonstrated influence, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills, including the ability to succeed within a matrix environment, are required. Design and synthesis of constrained macrocycles, de-peptidization strategies including back-bone modifications and peptidomimetics is required. Experience in peptide hit finding approaches – phage display, mRNA display technologies, etc. Cell penetrating peptides. Permeable and orally bioavailable peptides. Intracellular protein-protein interaction targets. Chemical biology using cyclic peptide scaffolds. Strong track record of scientific contributions including peer reviewed first-author publications, patent applications, and presentations at major national meetings is preferred.

The Peptide group within [Company name masked]'s Global Discovery Chemistry group is committed to delivering high-quality drug candidates across all Therapeutic Areas (TAs). This mission requires deep scientific expertise across chemistry, cellular and molecular pharmacology, enzymology, and screening technologies, along with the ability to work collaboratively with internal and external partners.
We are seeking an experienced, skilled chemist with strong peptide chemistry and medicinal chemistry expertise to shepherd peptide drug discovery programs and advance them toward the clinic. The Principal Scientist will partner with key stakeholders in the TAs and other internal groups, represent medicinal chemistry, lead cross-functional project teams, and be co-responsible for building, managing, and delivering high quality clinical molecules. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of peptide drug discovery and the science behind program progression.
cond_0166.responsibilities:
Of the Principal Scientist will include:
As a medicinal chemist, drive and contribute to the peptide chemistry function for one or more drug discovery projects, working in concert with partners in molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, computational chemistry, chemistry capabilities, ADME, structural biology, chemical development, and other key functions.
Work collaboratively with other [Company name masked] drug discovery sites, including [Location masked], [Location masked], [Location masked], and [Location masked], and with [Company name masked] Innovation Centers worldwide.
Analyze synthetic routes to designed compounds, screening data, perform literature reviews, design, propose, and execute medicinal chemistry plans, coordinate chemistry and biology data to support compound progression and patent strategies.
Independently designing and synthesizing drug-like peptide molecules utilizing current medicinal chemistry knowledge, including property-based optimization, and an understanding of ADME, pharmacokinetics and optimal physicochemical properties.
Provide scientific direction and leadership for synthetic and medicinal chemistry activities of internal FTEs. This role may have direct people management responsibilities.
Supervise and direct synthetic chemistry activities at contract research organizations (CROs).
Contribute to portfolio and stage-gate reviews, lead the preparation and presentation of dossiers for clinical candidate nomination and compound advancement.
Participate in shaping and implementing strategies that support synthetic and medicinal chemistry growth objectives at [Company name masked], including academic relations and talent acquisition.
Ensure optimal interaction/communication and provide updates on project status to drug discovery leadership.
Maintain a significant level of productivity in the laboratory setting.
cond_0166.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD in peptide, synthetic organic, or medicinal chemistry.
A minimum of 3 or more years' experience in the biopharmaceutical industry with a proven track record of key contributions to innovative peptide projects impacting the trajectory of programs leading to Go/NoGo decisions and/or clinical candidate selection.
Experience designing peptide conformational restraints to influence secondary structure (ie. A-helices, b-turn induction & mimicry, sidechain modifications) using computational modeling tools.
Good understanding of cellular/molecular biology, biochemistry, disease pharmacology, mechanisms of drug metabolism and molecular toxicology, pharmaco-kinetic and pharmaco-dynamic sciences, and formulations for the in vivo evaluation of drug candidates.
Knowledge of and/or experience with computational chemistry methods and biophysical techniques such as X-ray crystallography and macromolecular NMR.
Strong problem-solving skills for developing creative, innovative solutions, and meeting project objectives.
Demonstrated influence, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills, including the ability to succeed within a matrix environment.
Design and synthesis of constrained macrocycles, de-peptidization strategies including back-bone modifications and peptidomimetics.
Preferred Requirements
Broad experience and proven accomplishments in medicinal chemistry; experience in one or more therapeutic areas.
Demonstrated operational skills for contributing to discovery programs at the level of a senior chemist/team leader.
Experience in peptide hit finding approaches – phage display, mRNA display technologies, etc.
Cell penetrating peptides.
Permeable and orally bioavailable peptides.
Intracellular protein-protein interaction targets.
Chemical biology using cyclic peptide scaffolds.
Strong track record of scientific contributions including peer reviewed first-author publications, patent applications, and presentations at major national meetings.

cond_0189.responsibilities:

Coordinate and oversee synthetic chemistry activities at contract research organizations (CROs).
Contribute to portfolio and stage-gate reviews; help prepare and present dossiers for clinical candidate nomination and compound advancement.
Support the shaping and implementation of strategies for synthetic and medicinal chemistry growth, including academic relations and talent acquisition.
Share updates on project status with drug discovery leadership and help ensure clear communication across the team.
Maintain a meaningful level of hands-on productivity in the laboratory.

PhD in peptide, synthetic organic, or medicinal chemistry.

Experience designing peptide conformational restraints to influence secondary structure (e.g., α-helices, β-turn induction and mimicry, sidechain modifications) using computational modeling tools.
Knowledge of and/or experience with computational chemistry methods and biophysical techniques such as X-ray crystallography and macromolecular NMR.

Good understanding of cellular/molecular biology, biochemistry, disease pharmacology, mechanisms of drug metabolism and molecular toxicology, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic sciences, and formulations for in vivo evaluation of drug candidates.
Strong problem-solving skills for developing creative, innovative solutions and meeting project objectives.

Broad experience and accomplishments in medicinal chemistry; experience in one or more therapeutic areas.
Demonstrated operational skills for contributing to discovery programs at the level of a senior chemist or team leader.
Experience in peptide hit-finding approaches such as phage display and mRNA display technologies.
Experience with cell-penetrating peptides, permeable and orally bioavailable peptides, intracellular protein-protein interaction targets, and chemical biology using cyclic peptide scaffolds.

cond_0227.intro:
We are looking for a Principal Scientist to join our Global Discovery Chemistry team.
The Peptide group within Global Discovery Chemistry group is committed to the delivery of high-quality drug candidates working across all Therapeutic Areas (TAs). This mission requires deep scientific expertise in a number of disciplines including chemistry, cellular and molecular pharmacology, enzymology, and screening technologies coupled with an ability to work collaboratively with internal and external partners. Building on a strong legacy of success, we are currently seeking an outstanding individual to join our team as Scientist, Discovery Chemistry.
We are seeking an experienced, highly skilled, and motivated chemist with excellent peptide chemistry and medicinal chemistry expertise to shepherd peptide drug discovery programs and advance them toward the clinic. This position will require the candidate to possess and leverage deep knowledge and capabilities to deliver differentiated clinical candidates to the [Company name masked] product development pipeline within our Disease and Pathway Area Stronghold (DAS and PAS) strategy. cond_0227.responsibilities:
Of the Principal Scientist will include:
As a dynamic medicinal chemist, drive and contribute to the peptide chemistry function for one or more drug discovery projects, working in concert with partners in molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, computational chemistry, chemistry capabilities, ADME, structural biology, chemical development, and other key functions. Work collaboratively with other [Company name masked] drug discovery sites, including [Location masked], [Location masked], [Location masked], and [Location masked], and with [Company name masked] Innovation Centers worldwide. Analyze synthetic routes to designed compounds, screening data, perform literature reviews, design, propose, and execute medicinal chemistry plans, coordinate chemistry and biology data to support compound progression and patent strategies. Independently designing and synthesizing drug-like peptide molecules utilizing current medicinal chemistry knowledge, including property-based optimization, and an understanding of ADME, pharmacokinetics and optimal physicochemical properties. Provide scientific direction and leadership for synthetic and medicinal chemistry activities of internal FTEs. This role may have direct people management responsibilities. Supervise and direct synthetic chemistry activities at contract research organizations (CROs). Contribute to portfolio and stage-gate reviews, lead the preparation and presentation of dossiers for clinical candidate nomination and compound advancement. Participate in shaping and implementing strategies that support synthetic and medicinal chemistry growth objectives at [Company name masked], including academic relations and talent acquisition. Ensure optimal interaction/communication and provide updates on project status to drug discovery leadership. Maintain a significant level of productivity in the laboratory setting.
cond_0227.requirements: PhD required in peptide, synthetic organic, or medicinal chemistry; advanced degree strongly preferred. A minimum of 3 years of demonstrated expertise in the biopharmaceutical industry with a proven track record of key contributions to innovative peptide projects impacting the trajectory of programs leading to Go/NoGo decisions and/or clinical candidate selection. Extensive experience and proven accomplishments in medicinal chemistry is preferred; substantial experience in one or more therapeutic areas is preferred. Demonstrated operational skills for contributing to discovery programs at the level of a senior chemist/team leader are preferred. Deep expertise in designing peptide conformational restraints to influence secondary structure (ie. Exceptional problem-solving skills for developing creative, innovative solutions, and meeting project objectives are required. Demonstrated influence, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills, including the ability to succeed within a matrix environment, are required. Expertise in design and synthesis of constrained macrocycles, de-peptidization strategies including back-bone modifications and peptidomimetics is required. As a dynamic medicinal chemist, drive and contribute to the peptide chemistry function for one or more drug discovery projects, working in concert with partners in molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, computational chemistry, chemistry capabilities, ADME, structural biology, chemical development, and other key functions. Work collaboratively with other [Company name masked] drug discovery sites, including [Location masked], [Location masked], [Location masked], and [Location masked], and with [Company name masked] Innovation Centers worldwide. Analyze synthetic routes to designed compounds, screening data, perform literature reviews, design, propose, and execute medicinal chemistry plans, coordinate chemistry and biology data to support compound progression and patent strategies. Independently designing and synthesizing drug-like peptide molecules utilizing current medicinal chemistry knowledge, including property-based optimization, and an understanding of ADME, pharmacokinetics and optimal physicochemical properties. Provide scientific direction and leadership for synthetic and medicinal chemistry activities of internal FTEs. This role may have direct people management responsibilities. Supervise and direct synthetic chemistry activities at contract research organizations (CROs). Contribute to portfolio and stage-gate reviews, lead the preparation and presentation of dossiers for clinical candidate nomination and compound advancement. Participate in shaping and implementing strategies that support synthetic and medicinal chemistry growth objectives at [Company name masked], including academic relations and talent acquisition. Ensure optimal interaction/communication and provide updates on project status to drug discovery leadership. Maintain a significant level of productivity in the laboratory setting.
cond_0408.requirements:
PhD in peptide, synthetic organic, or medicinal chemistry is required. Around 3 or more years of experience in the biopharmaceutical industry, with a background in contributing to innovative peptide projects that have influenced program direction, Go/NoGo decisions, and/or clinical candidate selection. Broad experience in medicinal chemistry is preferred; experience in one or more therapeutic areas is preferred. Familiarity with operational skills for contributing to discovery programs at the level of a senior chemist/team leader is preferred.
Experience designing peptide conformational restraints to influence secondary structure (ie. A-helices, b-turn induction & mimicry, sidechain modifications) using computational modeling tools is required. Working knowledge of cellular/molecular biology, biochemistry, disease pharmacology, mechanisms of drug metabolism and molecular toxicology, pharmaco-kinetic and pharmaco-dynamic sciences, and formulations for the in vivo evaluation of drug candidates. Experience with computational chemistry methods and biophysical techniques such as X-ray crystallography and macromolecular NMR is required.
Ability to develop creative, innovative solutions and meet project objectives is required. Ability to communicate effectively, negotiate, and work through conflict, including within a matrix environment, is required.
cond_0408.encouragement_text:
Experience with design and synthesis of constrained macrocycles, de-peptidization strategies including back-bone modifications and peptidomimetics is required. Experience in peptide hit finding approaches – phage display, mRNA display technologies, etc. Background in cell penetrating peptides, permeable and orally bioavailable peptides, intracellular protein-protein interaction targets, and chemical biology using cyclic peptide scaffolds is valued. A track record of scientific contributions including peer reviewed first-author publications, patent applications, and presentations at major national meetings is preferred; candidates who are building this record are also encouraged to apply.
Important: Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply.

We are looking for a Principal Scientist to join our Global Discovery Chemistry team.
The Peptide group within Global Discovery Chemistry is committed to delivering high-quality drug candidates across all Therapeutic Areas (TAs). This mission requires deep scientific expertise across chemistry, cellular and molecular pharmacology, enzymology, and screening technologies, along with the ability to work with internal and external partners.
We are seeking an experienced, highly skilled chemist with strong peptide chemistry and medicinal chemistry expertise to own peptide drug discovery programs and drive them toward the clinic. This position requires deep knowledge and capabilities to deliver differentiated clinical candidates to the [Company name masked] product development pipeline within our Disease and Pathway Area Stronghold (DAS and PAS) strategy. Using a mix of internal and external resources, the Principal Scientist will lead coordination with key stakeholders in the TAs and other internal groups, represent medicinal chemistry, direct cross-functional project teams, and take accountability for building, managing, and delivering high-quality clinical molecules.
cond_0512.responsibilities: As a dynamic medicinal chemist, lead and execute the peptide chemistry function for one or more drug discovery projects, working in concert with partners in molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, computational chemistry, chemistry capabilities, ADME, structural biology, chemical development, and other key functions. Drive collaboration with other [Company name masked] drug discovery sites, including [Location masked], and with [Company name masked] Innovation Centers worldwide. Analyze synthetic routes to designed compounds, screening data, perform literature reviews, design, propose, and execute medicinal chemistry plans, and direct chemistry and biology data to support compound progression and patent strategies. Independently design and synthesize drug-like peptide molecules utilizing current medicinal chemistry knowledge, including property-based optimization, and an understanding of ADME, pharmacokinetics, and optimal physicochemical properties. Provide scientific direction and leadership for synthetic and medicinal chemistry activities of internal FTEs. This role may have direct people management responsibilities. Direct synthetic chemistry activities at contract research organizations (CROs). Contribute to portfolio and stage-gate reviews, lead the preparation and presentation of dossiers for clinical candidate nomination and compound advancement. Take ownership of shaping and implementing strategies that support synthetic and medicinal chemistry growth objectives at [Company name masked], including academic relations and talent acquisition. Ensure optimal interaction and communication, and deliver updates on project status to drug discovery leadership. Maintain a significant level of productivity in the laboratory setting.
cond_0512.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD in peptide, synthetic organic, or medicinal chemistry.
A minimum of 3 or more years' experience in the biopharmaceutical industry with a proven track record of key contributions to innovative peptide projects impacting the trajectory of programs leading to Go/NoGo decisions and/or clinical candidate selection.
Experience designing peptide conformational restraints to influence secondary structure (i.e. A-helices, b-turn induction & mimicry, sidechain modifications) using computational modeling tools.
Good understanding of cellular/molecular biology, biochemistry, disease pharmacology, mechanisms of drug metabolism and molecular toxicology, pharmaco-kinetic and pharmaco-dynamic sciences, and formulations for the in vivo evaluation of drug candidates.
Knowledge of and/or experience with computational chemistry methods and biophysical techniques such as X-ray crystallography and macromolecular NMR.
Strong problem-solving skills for developing creative, innovative solutions and meeting project objectives.
Demonstrated influence, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills, including the ability to succeed within a matrix environment.
Design and synthesis of constrained macrocycles, de-peptidization strategies including back-bone modifications and peptidomimetics.
Preferred Requirements
Broad experience and proven accomplishments in medicinal chemistry; experience in one or more therapeutic areas.
Demonstrated operational skills for contributing to discovery programs at the level of a senior chemist/team leader.
Experience in peptide hit finding approaches – phage display, mRNA display technologies, etc.
Cell penetrating peptides.
Permeable and orally bioavailable peptides.
Intracellular protein-protein interaction targets.
Chemical biology using cyclic peptide scaffolds.
Strong track record of scientific contributions including peer reviewed first-author publications, patent applications, and presentations at major national meetings.

cond_0513.intro:
We are looking for a Principal Scientist to join our Global Discovery Chemistry team, working within the Peptide group in Medicinal Chemistry at [Location masked].
The Peptide group is committed to delivering high-quality drug candidates across all Therapeutic Areas (TAs). This work draws on deep scientific expertise in chemistry, cellular and molecular pharmacology, enzymology, and screening technologies, and depends on close collaboration with internal and external partners. We are seeking an experienced chemist with strong peptide and medicinal chemistry expertise to help shepherd peptide drug discovery programs toward the clinic. The Principal Scientist will work alongside key stakeholders in the TAs and other internal groups, represent medicinal chemistry in cross-functional project teams, and share responsibility for building, managing, and delivering high-quality clinical molecules.
cond_0513.responsibilities:
As a medicinal chemist, you will contribute to the peptide chemistry function for one or more drug discovery projects, working in concert with partners in molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, computational chemistry, ADME, structural biology, chemical development, and other key functions. You will coordinate with other [Company name masked] drug discovery sites and Innovation Centers worldwide.
Working together with the team, you will:
Analyze synthetic routes to designed compounds, review screening data and literature, and help shape and execute medicinal chemistry plans; coordinate chemistry and biology data to support compound progression and patent strategies.
Collaborate on the design and synthesis of drug-like peptide molecules, applying current medicinal chemistry knowledge including property-based optimization and an understanding of ADME, pharmacokinetics, and physicochemical properties.
Provide scientific direction for synthetic and medicinal chemistry activities of internal FTEs. This role may include direct people management responsibilities.
Coordinate and oversee synthetic chemistry activities at contract research organizations (CROs).
Contribute to portfolio and stage-gate reviews; help prepare and present dossiers for clinical candidate nomination and compound advancement.
Support the shaping and implementation of strategies for synthetic and medicinal chemistry growth, including academic relations and talent acquisition.
Share updates on project status with drug discovery leadership and help ensure clear communication across the team.
Maintain a meaningful level of hands-on productivity in the laboratory.
cond_0513.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
PhD in peptide, synthetic organic, or medicinal chemistry.
At least 3 years of experience in the biopharmaceutical industry with a proven track record of contributions to innovative peptide projects, including impact on Go/NoGo decisions and/or clinical candidate selection.
Experience designing peptide conformational restraints to influence secondary structure (e.g., α-helices, β-turn induction and mimicry, sidechain modifications) using computational modeling tools.
Knowledge of and/or experience with computational chemistry methods and biophysical techniques such as X-ray crystallography and macromolecular NMR.
Design and synthesis of constrained macrocycles, de-peptidization strategies including backbone modifications and peptidomimetics.
Good understanding of cellular/molecular biology, biochemistry, disease pharmacology, mechanisms of drug metabolism and molecular toxicology, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic sciences, and formulations for in vivo evaluation of drug candidates.
Strong problem-solving skills for developing creative, innovative solutions and meeting project objectives.
Demonstrated influence, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills, including the ability to work effectively within a matrix environment.
Preferred Requirements
Broad experience and accomplishments in medicinal chemistry; experience in one or more therapeutic areas.
Demonstrated operational skills for contributing to discovery programs at the level of a senior chemist or team leader.
Experience in peptide hit-finding approaches such as phage display and mRNA display technologies.
Experience with cell-penetrating peptides, permeable and orally bioavailable peptides, intracellular protein-protein interaction targets, and chemical biology using cyclic peptide scaffolds.
Strong track record of scientific contributions including peer-reviewed first-author publications, patent applications, and presentations at major national meetings.

As a medicinal chemist, actively drive and contribute to the peptide chemistry function for one or more drug discovery projects, working closely and regularly with partners in molecular and cellular biology, pharmacology, computational chemistry, chemistry capabilities, ADME, structural biology, chemical development, and other key functions. Stay in regular contact and work collaboratively with other [Company name masked] drug discovery sites and with [Company name masked] Innovation Centers worldwide. Analyze synthetic routes to designed compounds, screening data, perform literature reviews, design, propose, and execute medicinal chemistry plans, and coordinate chemistry and biology data to support compound progression and patent strategies. Provide scientific direction and leadership for synthetic and medicinal chemistry activities of internal FTEs. This role may have direct people management responsibilities. Supervise and direct synthetic chemistry activities at contract research organizations (CROs). Actively contribute to portfolio and stage-gate reviews, lead the preparation and presentation of dossiers for clinical candidate nomination and compound advancement. Participate in shaping and implementing strategies that support synthetic and medicinal chemistry growth objectives at [Company name masked], including academic relations and talent acquisition. Initiate and maintain clear communication and provide regular updates on project status to drug discovery leadership. Maintain a significant level of productivity in the laboratory setting.
cond_0627.requirements: PhD is required in peptide, synthetic organic, or medicinal chemistry. Broad experience and proven accomplishments in medicinal chemistry is preferred; experience in one or more therapeutic areas is preferred. Demonstrated operational skills for contributing to discovery programs at the level of a senior chemist/team leader are preferred. Experience designing peptide conformational restraints to influence secondary structure (ie. A-helices, b-turn induction & mimicry, sidechain modifications) using computational modeling tools is required. Good understanding of cellular/molecular biology, biochemistry, disease pharmacology, mechanisms of drug metabolism and molecular toxicology, pharmaco-kinetic and pharmaco-dynamic sciences, and formulations for the in vivo evaluation of drug candidates. Knowledge of and/or experience with computational chemistry methods and biophysical techniques such as X-ray crystallography and macromolecular NMR is required. Strong problem-solving skills for developing creative, innovative solutions, and meeting project objectives are required. Demonstrated influence, negotiation, and conflict resolution skills, including the ability to succeed within a matrix environment, are required. Design and synthesis of constrained macrocycles, de-peptidization strategies including back-bone modifications and peptidomimetics is required. Experience in peptide hit finding approaches – phage display, mRNA display technologies, etc. Cell penetrating peptides. Permeable and orally bioavailable peptides. Strong track record of scientific contributions including peer reviewed first-author publications, patent applications, and presentations at major national meetings is preferred.
